newsitem.title: USA: Dlr ends near flat in US after overseas stumble.
newsitem.headline: Dlr ends near flat in US after overseas stumble.

text.p: Helped by strength in U.S. stocks and short-covering ahead of Europe's close, the dollar steadied to end the U.S. trading session narrowly mixed on Monday.

But the greenback remained substantially lower than Friday's closing levels after a sharp drop overnight and U.S. players were hesitant to push the dollar much higher ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semi-annual testimony to Congress, scheduled to begin on Wednesday.

Weighing on the dollar overseas were worries about a delay in Europe's plans for a single currency, which helped the mark, and fears that Japanese companies might sell large amounts of dollars ahead of their approaching fiscal year-end.

The dollar ended the session at 1.6730/35 marks, slightly below its opening level of 1.6740/50, but well below its Friday close of 1.6891/96. It settled at 122.13/18 yen, at tad up from 122.07/12 at the open, but off Friday's ending rate of 123.20/30.

"The stock market is up and that's probably adding a little bit of support," said Bob Near, vice president on the corporate foreign exchange desk at Bank of New York. "But the market was pre-disposed to taking some profits today."
The Dow Jones Industrials ended the day up over 76 points to close at around 7008.

The Japanese company Mitsubishi Heavy Industries said on Monday that it planned to liquidate all its dollar-denominated deposits, currently at around $700 million, and convert them into yen to make up shortfalls in cash.
This sparked concern that other Japanese companies might repatriate funds, as they have in previous years, ahead of Japan's fiscal year-end in March, boosting the yen.
The dollar's poor performance against the mark was a function of fresh doubts about the timetable for Europe's planned single currency.
A survey in the German magazine Der Spiegel showed over the weekend that 77 percent of Germans want Economic and Monetary Union delayed from its planned start date of 1999.

"There are increased concerns about EMU being delayed, and while it hasn't caused a rush into deutschemarks, its one more factor that is supporting some mark buying," said John McCarthy of ING Barings Capital Markets.
Traders said Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's upcoming Humphrey-Hawkins testimony kept the market cautious on Monday.
"There is a lot of concern about Humphrey-Hawkins," said Near. "There's a chance, given Greenspan's irrational exuberance concerns of the past, that he could send the markets for a loop."

Greenspan, who will give his assessment of the U.S. economy to the Senate Banking Committee this Wednesday and the House Banking Committee on March 5, sent global markets reeling last December when he spoke of "irrational exuberance" in U.S. asset markets.
In other trade on Monday, the dollar ended slightly lower at 1.4572/77 Swiss francs against 1.4580/90 at the open. The British pound rose to $1.6352/57 versus $1.6268/78 in early trade.
The dollar was steady at Canadian $1.3618/23 versus C$1.3616/21 and the Australian dollar closed at $0.7765/70.
